question_en: Investors who are less risk averse will have what type of indifference curves for risk and expected return?
explanation_en: Investors who are less risk averse will have flatter indifference curves, meaning they are willing to take on more risk for a slightly higher return. Investors who are more risk averse require a much higher return to accept more risk, producing steeper indifference curves.

question_en: Which of the following statements best describes an investment that is not on the efficient frontier?
option_a: There is a portfolio that has a lower return for the same risk.
option_b: The portfolio has a very high return.
option_c: There is a portfolio that has a lower risk for the same return.
explanation_en: The efficient frontier outlines the set of portfolios that gives investors the highest return for a given level of risk or the lowest risk for a given level of return. Therefore, if a portfolio is not on the efficient frontier, there must be a portfolio that has lower risk for the same return. Equivalently, there must be a portfolio that produces a higher return for the same risk.

explanation_en: Because there is a perfectly positive correlation, there is no benefit to diversification. Therefore, the investor should put all his money into Stock A (with the lowest standard deviation) to minimize the risk (standard deviation) of the portfolio.

question_en: A line that represents the possible portfolios that combine a risky asset and a risk free asset is most accurately described as a:
explanation_en: The line that represents possible combinations of a risky asset and the risk-free asset is referred to as a capital allocation line (CAL). The capital market line (CML) represents possible combinations of the market portfolio with the risk-free asset. A characteristic line is the best fitting linear relationship between excess returns on an asset and excess returns on the market and is used to estimate an asset's beta.

question_en: Which of the following statements about portfolio theory is least accurate?
option_a: Assuming that the correlation coefficient is less than one, the risk of the portfolio will always be less than the simple weighted average of individual stock risks.
option_b: For a two-stock portfolio, the lowest risk occurs when the correlation coefficient is close to negative one.
option_c: When the return on an asset added to a portfolio has a correlation coefficient of less than one with the other portfolio asset returns but has the same risk, adding the asset will not decrease the overall portfolio standard deviation.
explanation_en: When the return on an asset added to a portfolio has a correlation coefficient of less than one with the other portfolio asset returns but has the same risk, adding the asset will decrease the overall portfolio standard deviation. Any time the correlation coefficient is less than one, there are benefits from diversification. The other choices are true.
